prompt:
Find the documentation describing intended behavior for the codebase at target, and the code it describes.
The user pointed at target/DESIGN.md — start there, and include anything else that also specifies behavior.

Documentation is whatever states what the system is supposed to do: a whitepaper, a design note, a README section,
a protocol description, doc comments carrying real semantics. Judge by content, not filename. Skip changelogs,
contributor guides, build instructions, and license text — they describe the project, not its behavior.

If a file plainly holds a specification but you cannot read it as text, record it under 'unreadable' rather than
guessing at its contents.

documents.description: Files that describe intended behavior, most authoritative first.

describes.description: what part of the system this document specifies

unreadable.description: Set only if the file could not be read as text (e.g. a binary .docx with no converter available). Name the file and why.

codePaths.description: Directories or files holding the implementation these documents describe.
